title: Review output
description: What one specialist reviewer returns. A finding is one description, optionally one suggestion, anchored at a line or a line range. Contract: docs/agents/review-contract.md

agent.description: Who is speaking. Set by the run from the axis it launched, not by the model: the review attributes each comment.

skipped.description: In-scope files this reviewer did not actually review, and why. Silence about coverage reads as full coverage.

severity.description: blocking = breaks behaviour, leaks data, or blocks a rollback. Also sets your word budget.

line.description: First line of the finding, in the HEAD version of the file. Must fall inside one of the `lines` ranges you were given for this file, or the finding cannot be attached to the code and is listed in the review body instead.

endLine.description: Last line, when the finding spans a range. The comment then covers line..endLine, which is what makes a multi-line suggestion readable. Omit for a single line. `line` and `endLine` must sit inside the SAME `lines` range: a span across two hunks cannot be posted.

description.description: The whole finding, in one field. No title, no separate rationale. Length is capped by severity: blocking 2 sentences, important 1, nit a few words. Say what is wrong and what breaks; stop there.

suggestion.description: Optional. One sentence, or a ```suggestion fenced block with the replacement code for line..endLine — the code form is preferred and is exempt from the sentence limit, but keep it minimal; pseudo-code is often enough. The block replaces line..endLine wholesale, so it need not have the same number of lines, and is passed through to GitHub verbatim.

evidence.description: Short verbatim quote of the offending code. Never rendered in the review: it exists so you cannot report what you have not read.

confidence.description: confirmed = you read the surrounding code and the failure holds. plausible = it looks wrong from the diff alone.

ruleId.description: The rule this finding cites, exactly as the `id` given in the input's `rules` list: `<doc>.md#<anchor>` for an anchored rule, or the rule file's path for a filed one. Required for blocking and important; omitted for an unanchored nit. Cite only a rule your axis owns.
